dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: Discipline is the backbone and lifeblood of an army. Those who cannot watch their mouths in school will prove to be fodder in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the instructor here, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: That's right, I'm the current Head Instructor of the Royal Military Academy, Lukyana Vasilyevna Dragomirova, Officer Third Class.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: As you can see, my duty is to forge these youngsters into blades to be wielded for our Tsaritsa, to protect our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: If you're not a student here, please don't stay for too long, or you may interfere with the normal flow of classes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me a bit about the Academy...

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: I'm no bard. If you want to hear stories, I suggest you hear them at the Podvorye Restaurant.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: I can only tell you what sort of place this is. This was once a club for the nobility, which only fae and the children of high-ranking military officers could enroll in.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: Only when Her Majesty took the throne did it start to have a quota for enrolling commoners. That said, prejudice and discrimination have proved tough to break down.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: Even now, we still get some noble whelps, far too big for their britches, who need to be taught the meaning of "egalitarian discipline" from the comfort of solitary confinement.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, where do graduates from this place go?

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: The aristocrats usually inherit their family businesses afterward, while the vast majority of commoners join the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: For the latter group, this is the best way to climb the ladder and gain merit.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: It is the highest honor to sacrifice themselves for Her Majesty. It's just... some recent Fatui policies, and the manner in which some Harbinger operate...

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: ...Must they really take these children, freshly out of their graduation uniforms, to replace those lost to meaningless sacrifices?

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: Sorry, I spoke out of turn. Just consider these the pointless ramblings of an old woman.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Lukyana
dialogues.text: See you.
